title: Semester and Scholarship
premise: Casper Nystrom, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has survived three years by being invisible — until the senior college essay prompt asks students to write about a truth that changed them, and his honest draft is accidentally read aloud in class. The essay exposes the secret he's guarded since arriving: he's been quietly funding his mother's medical bills with money skimmed from the school's tutoring program, a system built by his best friend Priya's family. As the administration investigates and Priya feels betrayed, Casper must decide whether to lie his way to graduation or tell the whole truth at the winter scholarship audition that determines his future. He tells the truth, loses the scholarship, but gains an unexpected found family — including Priya's forgiveness — when the student body rallies to fund his final semester.
about_author: Beatrix Winterbourne is the pen name of a former boarding school teacher who spent a decade watching brilliant students hide how much they were carrying. She writes young adult fiction about kids who learn that survival isn't the same as living. She lives near the coast with two rescue cats and an unreasonable number of annotated paperbacks.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Opening day of senior year at Ashgrove Academy; we see his careful invisibility routine — perfect grades, no clubs, no questions. He checks his hidden ledger of tutoring money sent home for his mother's treatment. Emotional beat: controlled anxiety, the cost of staying small.

chapters.title: The Locker Rule
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback woven into present: how freshman-year Casper learned never to let anyone close after a roommate discovered his free-lunch status and spread it around. Establishes Priya as the one exception — a friendship built on her never asking about money. Beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. English teacher Mr. Okafor assigns the college essay: 'Describe a truth that changed you.' Casper writes honestly for the first time in years, alone at midnight, telling himself it will never be submitted. Beat: dangerous relief, the intoxication of honesty.

chapters.title: Priya's Empire
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. We meet the Raghavan family's tutoring program — a student-run service Priya built that Casper administers. Priya trusts Casper completely; she's planning to expand it into a formal scholarship fund. Dramatic irony tightens: she praises his 'impeccable books.' Beat: warmth shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Mix-Up
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. During peer-review workshop, Mr. Okafor accidentally projects Casper's unsubmitted draft instead of the sample essay. Forty students hear Casper describe skimming money from a program 'run by someone who trusts me.' Beat: public exposure, stomach-drop horror.

chapters.title: Forty Pairs of Eyes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The fallout in the hallway; Priya confronts Casper, hurt more by the secrecy than the theft. Casper can't explain about his mother without sounding like an excuse. Their friendship fractures publicly. Beat: betrayal on both sides, neither fully wrong.

chapters.title: What the Money Was For
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A phone call home reveals his mother's condition worsening; we finally see the full weight he carries — hospital invoices, a father who left, a younger brother. The reader understands before the school does. Beat: sympathy deepens, stakes clarify.

chapters.title: Dean Harrow Summons You
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The administration opens a quiet investigation; Dean Harrow offers a deal — full confession and withdrawal, or expulsion and a mark on his record that kills every college acceptance. Casper has one week. Beat: institutional menace, powerlessness.

chapters.title: The Audition Clause
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya learns the winter scholarship audition — her family endows it — could still save Casper if he performs and speaks truthfully about his circumstances. She wrestles with whether to help him or protect her program's reputation. Beat: conflicted loyalty.

chapters.title: Allies in Strange Places
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Unexpected classmates — Theo the theater kid, quiet Marisol, even the boy who once mocked him — begin circling Casper, each carrying their own hidden costs of attending Ashgrove. The first hints of found family. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Honesty
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo coaches Casper for the audition piece — not just performance, but emotional truth. Casper keeps flinching from the real story. Theo shares why he transferred schools twice. Beat: vulnerability practiced in safe company.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper reconstructs exactly what he took and why, preparing a full accounting for the board. Revisiting three years of decisions, he stops seeing himself as purely victim or thief. Beat: moral reckoning, self-forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Priya Reads the File
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds the hospital records Casper left in the program office and finally understands the whole picture — including that he'd been repaying the money secretly from weekend work. Her anger cracks into grief. Beat: empathy breaking through resentment.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Someone leaks the investigation to the student paper; the school turns Casper's story into gossip and spectacle. Marisol, editor, must choose between the scoop and the person. She sits on the story. Beat: solidarity versus ambition.

chapters.title: Winter Audition Eve
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The night before the audition, Dean Harrow pressures Casper to withdraw quietly, hinting the board has already decided. Casper nearly accepts — then gets a call that his mother is stable, and something in him refuses to shrink anymore. Beat: the turn from survival to courage.

chapters.title: The Truth, Aloud
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Climax part one: Casper auditions, abandoning his prepared piece to tell the entire story — the money, the mother, the shame, the friendship he broke. The room goes silent. Beat: raw catharsis, the essay prompt answered for real.

chapters.title: What the Board Decided
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board revokes the scholarship anyway — rules are rules — but Priya stands before them and resigns stewardship of her family's fund rather than endorse the decision. Beat: costly integrity mirroring Casper's own.

chapters.title: The Loudest Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Aftermath: Casper packs his locker, expecting nothing, when students begin appearing — Theo, Marisol, half the senior class — with an organized fund they started without him. Priya arrives last. Beat: overwhelming grace, tears finally allowed.

chapters.title: Terms of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Priya and Casper's alternating POV. Priya doesn't excuse him; she names what he owes — honesty going forward, restitution finished, no more disappearing. Casper agrees. They rebuild slowly, awkwardly, honestly. Beat: reconciliation earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: Semester Two
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The student-funded semester begins; Casper joins the tutoring program openly, teaching younger scholarship kids the survival skills he wishes he'd had. His mother video-calls during a session, laughing. Beat: identity transformed from hiding to belonging.

chapters.title: The Essay, Revised
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper resubmits his college essay — the true version, signed. Mr. Okafor reads it and tells him it's the finest thing a student has handed him in twenty years. Acceptance letters begin arriving. Beat: quiet triumph, the question answered.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, brief rotating sections. Graduation eve: each friend leaves something in Casper's now-open locker — notes, a photo, Priya's repaired ledger with a new page titled 'Even.' Final image: Casper walking out of Ashgrove with his head up. Beat: resolution, found family secured, identity claimed.
